title: A telescope with a longer objective
hook: Change objective focal length and predict angular magnification magnitude.
misconception: angular magnification magnitude stays fixed when objective focal length doubles.
objective: Apply magnification magnitude = f_objective/f_eyepiece to compare angular magnification magnitude when objective focal length changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an ideal astronomical telescope with fixed eyepiece focal length, magnification magnitude = f_objective/f_eyepiece. When objective focal length doubles, angular magnification magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model magnification magnitude = f_objective/f_eyepiece; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an ideal astronomical telescope with fixed eyepiece focal length, with a nonzero initial result. If objective focal length triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on angular magnification magnitude?
recall.why: Apply magnification magnitude = f_objective/f_eyepiece under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
